question: What is the main reason healthcare providers use drug classification systems?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for doctor prescriptions
options.B: To help nurses administer medications safely and anticipate effects
options.C: To ensure all medications cost the same amount of money
options.D: To make drug manufacturing companies produce fewer pills

explanation: Grouping drugs helps nurses predict how a medication will work and watch out for specific side effects during patient care. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why might a single medication belong to more than one distinct category?

options.A: Because it can be classified by its chemical structure or disease treated
options.B: Because doctors use random methods to sort medications
options.C: Because drug companies change the name of the drug every year
options.D: Because government laws require multiple names for safety

explanation: A drug can be sorted differently based on how it is made, how it acts in the body, or the specific illness it targets. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h1)

question: What does the therapeutic use of a medication describe?

options.A: The chemical formula written on the manufacturing bottle
options.B: The exact physical size and color of the pill
options.C: The specific disease or condition the drug is used to treat
options.D: The country where the medication was originally made

explanation: Therapeutic use refers to the clinical condition or illness that the drug is meant to manage or cure. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h2)

question: How does pharmacological action differ from therapeutic use?

options.A: It explains how the drug works in the body rather than what disease it treats
options.B: It tells the nurse how many pills the patient should swallow
options.C: It describes the financial cost of producing the medication
options.D: It is only used by pharmacists and never looked at by nurses

explanation: Pharmacological action focuses on the cellular or body mechanism, while therapeutic use focuses on the target illness. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why do prescription medications require a doctor's order?

options.A: They carry higher risks and require medical supervision
options.B: They do not cause any side effects in patients
options.C: They can only be manufactured in hospital pharmacies
options.D: They are always much cheaper than other medications

explanation: Prescription drugs have powerful effects or serious risks that need professional oversight for safe use. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient tells a nurse they only take 'natural' painkillers bought off the supermarket shelf. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient that shop-bought drugs do not count as real medication
options.B: Ignore the information since a prescription was not required
options.C: Document and review the OTC use for potential drug interactions
options.D: Immediately report the patient to the hospital pharmacy board

explanation: Even OTC drugs can interact with prescription treatments, so nurses must document and evaluate all self-administered products. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main characteristic of a Schedule I controlled substance?

options.A: High potential for abuse and no accepted medical use
options.B: Used only in emergency rooms for sudden cardiac arrest
options.C: Low risk of addiction and available over-the-counter
options.D: Safe enough to be given without any professional oversight

explanation: Schedule I drugs have the highest abuse potential and are not approved for standard medical treatment. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why do hospitals enforce strict double-key storage and witness counts for narcotics?

options.A: To prevent drug diversion and control abuse risks
options.B: To make medication administration take longer for nurses
options.C: To test whether the patient actually needs pain relief
options.D: To ensure the pharmaceutical company makes more profit

explanation: Strict counting and witness rules protect controlled substances from theft, misuse, or illegal diversion. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is a common misconception about herbal and complementary medications?

options.A: They can only be bought with a doctor's prescription
options.B: They are chemically identical to synthetic antibiotics
options.C: They never interact with standard hospital drugs
options.D: They are completely harmless because they are natural

explanation: Patients often think natural means safe, but herbs contain active chemicals that can cause serious side effects or drug interactions. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why must nurses specifically ask about herbal supplements during a medication history check?

options.A: Hospitals require patients to buy herbal tea during admission
options.B: Herbs can change how prescription drugs work in the body
options.C: Doctors use herbs to replace all standard intravenous fluids
options.D: Herbs are legally classified as Schedule I controlled substances

explanation: Herbal products can speed up or slow down drug metabolism, leading to unexpected treatment failures or toxicity. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which clinical situation typically requires the administration of emergency and critical care drugs?

options.A: Discharge planning for a patient with a healed fracture
options.B: Annual physical checkup in a healthy adult client
options.C: A sudden, life-threatening crisis like cardiac arrest
options.D: Routine outpatient follow-up for chronic mild headache

explanation: Emergency drugs are reserved for critical, unstable situations where rapid intervention is necessary to save a life. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why do critical care medications require exceptionally close monitoring by the nurse?

options.A: They can only be stored inside patient bedside lockers
options.B: They act very rapidly and have powerful effects on the body
options.C: They do not require any dose calculation before giving
options.D: They are usually very inexpensive to purchase in bulk

explanation: Because critical care drugs work fast and powerfully, small dosage errors can quickly lead to dangerous patient complications. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h6)

question: What defines an orphan drug?

options.A: A medication developed to treat a rare medical condition
options.B: An herbal supplement with no scientific research backing
options.C: A controlled substance classified under Schedule I rules
options.D: A drug that has been abandoned by the manufacturing company

explanation: Orphan drugs are specifically created to help patients suffering from rare diseases that affect few people. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why do pharmaceutical companies often need special incentives to develop orphan drugs?

options.A: Rare disease medications are made only from plant roots
options.B: Doctors refuse to prescribe drugs that treat uncommon illnesses
options.C: Government laws forbid selling rare disease drugs for money
options.D: The small number of patients makes traditional profit difficult

explanation: Developing a drug costs millions, but with very few patients to buy it, companies need incentives to offset research costs. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h7)
